title: String Concatenation
learning_outcomes: Explain the purpose of string concatenation and identify when it is appropriate in a Java program.
Apply at least one of the lesson topics—the + operator—in a small, readable example.
Predict the example result and check it against the stated output or a boundary-case test.

content.intro: In this lesson, you will study string concatenation with a short explanation, an original visual map, a Java example, and a check you can perform yourself. Focus on the relationship between the rule and the behavior rather than memorizing isolated syntax.
content.why_it_matters: This concept matters because it helps you process text correctly while accounting for immutability, equality, and Unicode. In this lesson, focus on the + operator and use a minimal example to check what the rule actually guarantees.

content_blocks.title: The core idea
content_blocks.text: Operator precedence and numeric promotion determine the resulting value. Make conversions explicit when narrowing a type, and test integer boundaries and floating-point rounding instead of assuming arithmetic is exact. The important habit is to make the assumptions explicit and use the code example as a small experiment.

content_blocks.title: How the pieces fit
content_blocks.text: Connect the + operator with concat() before choosing an implementation. The example is a small, observable case; extend it by changing one input and checking a boundary, invalid value, or compatibility limit where relevant.

items.title: The + operator
items.text: Operator precedence and numeric promotion determine the resulting value. Make conversions explicit when narrowing a type, and test integer boundaries and floating-point rounding instead of assuming arithmetic is exact.

items.title: concat()
items.text: String values are immutable, so methods return new results rather than changing existing text. Compare contents with `equals`, and distinguish UTF-16 code units from Unicode code points and visible graphemes. Apply that reasoning specifically to concat() and confirm the result with the example or a targeted test.

items.title: Combining variables and literals
items.text: A variable has a declared type and a scope. Initialize local variables before reading them; fields have defined default values, but relying on defaults can hide missing business logic.

items.title: Formatting versus concatenation
items.text: String values are immutable sequences of text. Use value equality for text content, understand Unicode code points for international text, and prefer StringBuilder for repeated concatenation in loops.
